title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram

title: 0/1 Knapsack Problem & Subset Sum
problem_statement: Given weights and values of N items, put these items in a knapsack of capacity W to get the maximum total value in the knapsack. In other words, given two integer arrays val[0..N-1] and wt[0..N-1] which represent values and weights associated with N items respectively, find the maximum value subset such that the sum of the weights of this subset is smaller than or equal to W.
sample_io: Input: N = 3, W = 4, values = [1,2,3], weights = [4,5,1]. Output: 3.
expected_solution: Dynamic Programming: State `dp[i][w]` is max value achievable using a subset of first `i` items with capacity `w`. Transition: `dp[i][w] = max(dp[i-1][w], val[i-1] + dp[i-1][w - wt[i-1]])`. Space optimized to a 1D array of size `W+1` iterated in reverse order from W down to wt[i-1]. Time: O(N * W), Space: O(W).

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
problem_statement: There is an integer array nums sorted in ascending order (with distinct values). Prior to being passed to your function, nums is possibly rotated at an unknown pivot index k. Given the array nums after the possible rotation and an integer target, return the index of target if it is in nums, or -1 if it is not in nums. You must write an algorithm with O(log n) runtime complexity.
sample_io: Input: nums = [4,5,6,7,0,1,2], target = 0. Output: 4. Input: nums = [4,5,6,7,0,1,2], target = 3. Output: -1.
expected_solution: Modified Binary Search. Calculate mid. Determine whether the left half [low...mid] or right half [mid...high] is sorted. If left half is sorted, check if target falls in `nums[low] <= target < nums[mid]`. If so, search left (`high = mid - 1`); otherwise search right. If right half is sorted, apply symmetric logic. Time: O(log N), Space: O(1).
followups: Follow-up: What if duplicates are allowed (e.g. [2,5,6,0,0,1,2])? Discuss how duplicates degrade worst-case runtime to O(N).

section: Part I: Most Frequent DSA Questions (Past 5 Years)
title: Detect and Remove Loop in a Linked List
problem_statement: Given the head of a linked list, check if the list has a loop in it. If a loop is present, detect the starting point of the loop and unlink it to restore the list to a linear singly linked list.
sample_io: Input: 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 3 (loop back to 3). Output: List restored to 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> null.
expected_solution: Floyd's Cycle Detection Algorithm (Tortoise and Hare). Slow pointer advances by 1 step, fast by 2 steps. If they meet, a loop exists. Reset slow pointer to head, keep fast pointer at meeting point; advance both by 1 step until they meet at loop origin. To remove: find the previous node before loop start and set its next to null. Time: O(N), Space: O(1).
followups: Follow-up: Provide a mathematical proof for why the distance from head to loop origin equals the distance from meeting point to loop origin.

section: Part I: Most Frequent DSA Questions (Past 5 Years)
title: Find Median from Data Stream

expected_solution: Two Priority Queues (Heaps): Max-Heap for the smaller lower half of numbers, and Min-Heap for the larger upper half of numbers. Balance sizes such that max-heap has at most 1 more element than min-heap. `addNum`: O(log N). `findMedian`: O(1). Overall Space: O(N).
followups: Follow-up: What if 99% of all numbers are in the range [0, 100]? What if 99% are positive integers up to 1000? Discuss Bucket/Count Array optimizations.

section: Part II: Microsoft Operating Systems & Concurrency Questions
title: Virtual Memory, Paging, and Thrashing
problem_statement: Explain page tables, translation lookaside buffers (TLB), and demand paging. What causes virtual memory thrashing, and how does the operating system detect and resolve it?Key Expected Answer Elements:• Thrashing occurs when CPU spends more time swapping pages in and out of secondary storage than executing user processes.• Cause: Sum of working sets of active processes exceeds physical RAM capacity.• Resolution: Working Set Model (Peter Denning), page fault frequency (PFF) monitoring, process suspension/swapping out to reduce multiprogramming degree.

section: Part II: Microsoft Operating Systems & Concurrency Questions
title: Deadlocks: The 4 Coffman Conditions and Prevention
problem_statement: Enumerate the 4 necessary and sufficient conditions for Deadlock. Explain Banker's Algorithm and how modern kernels (Windows NT, Linux) handle deadlocks in practice.Key Expected Answer Elements:• 4 Conditions: Mutual Exclusion, Hold and Wait, No Preemption, Circular Wait.• Prevention Strategies: Lock ordering hierarchy (prevents Circular Wait), acquiring all locks atomically at once.• Reality: Most general-purpose OS kernels use the Ostrich algorithm (ignore potential deadlocks at kernel level) and rely on timeouts, deadlock detection threads, and user-space watchdog timers.

section: Part II: Microsoft Operating Systems & Concurrency Questions
title: Concurrency Primitives: Spinlocks vs Mutexes vs Semaphores
problem_statement: Differentiate between Spinlocks, Mutexes, and Counting Semaphores. In what scenarios would a spinlock be chosen over a mutex in the Windows kernel?Key Expected Answer Elements:• Spinlock: Busy-waits in a tight loop burning CPU cycles. Used in kernel interrupt handlers (IRQL >= DISPATCH_LEVEL in Windows) where thread sleeping/context-switching is illegal, and lock hold times are guaranteed to be extremely short (nanoseconds).• Mutex: Puts thread to sleep when contended, waking it up via scheduler when released. Incurs context-switch overhead (microseconds).• Semaphore: Signaling primitive with counter allowing up to N concurrent threads.

title: Base Conversion without Standard Library Functions
problem_statement: Given a positive decimal integer N, write a program to convert it into its binary, octal, and hexadecimal representations without using language conversion helper functions (such as `Integer.toHexString` or `bin()`).
sample_io: Input: N = 45. Output: Binary = 101101, Octal = 55, Hexadecimal = 2D.

section: Part I: Most Frequent Coding Questions (TCS Ninja & Digital)
title: Longest Palindromic Substring
problem_statement: Given a string s, return the longest palindromic substring in s.
sample_io: Input: s = 'babad'. Output: 'bab' (or 'aba'). Input: s = 'cbbd'. Output: 'bb'. Constraints: length <= 1000.
expected_solution: Approach 1 (Center Expansion): For each index i, expand outwards checking both odd-length palindromes (center at i) and even-length palindromes (center between i and i+1). Time: O(N^2), Space: O(1).Approach 2 (Dynamic Programming): Table `dp[i][j]` is true if substring from i to j is palindrome. Transition: `dp[i][j] = (s[i] == s[j]) && dp[i+1][j-1]` (Time: O(N^2), Space: O(N^2)).
followups: Follow-up: What algorithm achieves O(N) linear time for this problem? (Discuss Manacher's Algorithm).

section: Part I: Most Frequent Coding Questions (TCS Ninja & Digital)
title: Coin Change Problem (Minimum Coins)
problem_statement: You are given an integer array coins representing coins of different denominations and an integer amount representing a total amount of money. Return the fewest number of coins that you need to make up that amount. If that amount of money cannot be made up by any combination of the coins, return -1. You may assume you have an infinite number of each kind of coin.
expected_solution: Unbounded Knapsack / Dynamic Programming: 1D array `dp` of size `amount + 1` initialized to infinity (`amount + 1`), with `dp[0] = 0`. For `i` from 1 to `amount`, for each coin `c` in `coins`: if `i - c >= 0`, `dp[i] = min(dp[i], 1 + dp[i - c])`. If `dp[amount] > amount`, return -1. Time: O(amount * len(coins)), Space: O(amount).
followups: Follow-up: Why does a Greedy approach (always taking the largest denomination first) fail for denominations like [1, 3, 4] with amount = 6?

expected_solution: Maintain four boundary pointers: `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`. Traverse top row left-to-right (increment top), right column top-to-bottom (decrement right), bottom row right-to-left (decrement bottom, checking top <= bottom), and left column bottom-to-top (increment left, checking left <= right). Repeat until boundaries cross. Time: O(M * N), Space: O(1).

title: Trapping Rain Water
problem_statement: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
expected_solution: Two-Pointer Technique: Initialize `left = 0`, `right = n - 1`, `left_max = 0`, `right_max = 0`. While `left < right`: if `height[left] <= height[right]`, if `height[left] >= left_max`, update `left_max = height[left]`; else add `left_max - height[left]` to total water; advance `left++`. Symmetric logic for `right`. Time: O(N), Space: O(1).
followups: Follow-up: How does this compare with the Monotonic Stack approach?

section: Part II: C / C++ / Java Language Fundamentals & Pointer Traps
title: Pointers, Dangling Pointers, and Memory Leaks
problem_statement: Define what a pointer is. Differentiate between a NULL pointer, Void pointer, Wild pointer, and Dangling pointer with code examples.• Dangling Pointer: A pointer pointing to a memory location that has been deallocated/freed (`free(ptr);` without setting `ptr = NULL;`). Accessing it invokes undefined behavior.• Wild Pointer: An uninitialized pointer that points to an arbitrary arbitrary memory address.• Memory Leak: Allocated heap memory (`malloc`/`new`) that is no longer referenced but has not been freed, leading to progressive RAM exhaustion.• Smart Pointers in C++11: `std::unique_ptr` (exclusive ownership), `std::shared_ptr` (reference-counted ownership), `std::weak_ptr` (breaks circular references).

section: Part II: C / C++ / Java Language Fundamentals & Pointer Traps
title: Call by Value vs Call by Reference
problem_statement: Explain the internal parameter passing mechanisms in C, C++, and Java.• C: Strictly Call by Value. To simulate call by reference, explicit memory addresses are passed as pointer values.• C++: Supports both Call by Value and native Call by Reference (`void swap(int &a, int &b)`).• Java: Strictly Call by Value ALWAYS. When an object is passed, what is passed by value is the copy of the object reference (memory address), not the actual object itself. Reassigning the parameter variable inside the method does not affect the caller's reference.

section: Part II: C / C++ / Java Language Fundamentals & Pointer Traps
title: Static Keyword in C vs Java
problem_statement: What are the distinct meanings of the `static` keyword in C vs Java?• In C: (1) Inside a function: preserves variable value across successive function calls. (2) At file/global level: restricts linkage to the translation unit (file scope encapsulation).• In Java: Belongs to the class rather than instances. Used for static variables (shared across instances), static methods (cannot access `this` or instance variables), static nested classes, and static initializer blocks.

title: Find the Missing Number in 1 to N Array
problem_statement: Given an array nums containing n distinct numbers in the range [0, n], return the only number in the range that is missing from the array.
sample_io: Input: nums = [3,0,1]. Output: 2. Input: nums = [9,6,4,2,3,5,7,0,1]. Output: 8.
expected_solution: Method 1 (Sum Formula): Expected sum = `n * (n + 1) // 2`. Subtract array elements from expected sum (Time: O(N), Space: O(1)). Beware integer overflow for huge N. Method 2 (Bitwise XOR - Overflow proof): XOR all numbers from 0 to n, and XOR with array elements. Matching numbers cancel out leaving the missing number. Time: O(N), Space: O(1).
followups: Follow-up: What if two numbers are missing instead of one? (Discuss sum + product equations or XOR partitioning).

title: Check for Balanced Parentheses
problem_statement: Given a string s containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid.
sample_io: Input: s = '()[]{}'. Output: true. Input: s = '(]'. Output: false.
expected_solution: Stack data structure. Iterate through string. When opening bracket is encountered, push corresponding closing bracket onto stack. When closing bracket is encountered, verify `!stack.empty() && stack.pop() == char`. Valid if stack is empty at end. Time: O(N), Space: O(N).
followups: Follow-up: Can you optimize memory if string only contains a single type of bracket, like '(' and ')'? (Yes, simple integer counter in O(1) space).

title: Merge Two Sorted Linked Lists

expected_solution: Dummy Head Pointer + Two Pointers. Compare current nodes of list1 and list2, attach smaller node to tail, advance pointer. Attach remaining non-null sublist at end. Time: O(N + M), Space: strictly O(1) in-place.
followups: Follow-up: How do you merge K sorted linked lists? (Min-Heap / Priority Queue in O(N log K)).

title: Fibonacci Numbers: Recursion vs Memoization vs Space-Optimized DP
problem_statement: Write functions to calculate the Nth Fibonacci number using: (1) Naive Recursion, (2) Top-down Memoization, (3) Bottom-up DP with O(1) space.
expected_solution: Naive Recursion: O(2^N) time, O(N) stack space. Memoization (DP): O(N) time, O(N) space. Space-Optimized DP: Maintain two variables `prev2 = 0`, `prev1 = 1`; loop `curr = prev1 + prev2; prev2 = prev1; prev1 = curr;`. Time: O(N), Space: strictly O(1). Matrix Exponentiation achieves O(log N).
followups: Follow-up: What is the maximum value of N before 64-bit integer overflow occurs?
